title: FM-84, Atlas (album cover)
lede: James White’s cover for FM-84’s 2016 album: one huge striped sun, yellow at the top and magenta at the bottom, above a band of neon horizon lines on a starry night.
summary: A striped yellow-to-magenta sun on a starry navy sky, neon horizon lines below. James White, 2016.

source.label: Dribbble: FM-84: Atlas by James White

evidence.note: Inspected the 1200 px front-cover image from the [Cover Art Archive](https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/77f48f84-3d95-4e57-aae0-2d0d80dc7626) in a scratch folder. Not stored. The artwork credit is from the [Discogs record of the 2016 self-released digital edition](https://www.discogs.com/release/11581585-FM-84-Atlas).

styles.note: The retrosun alone: a striped yellow-to-magenta disc on a navy starry sky, which is the motif in its most reduced, iconic form.

context: Discogs records *Atlas* as a self-released digital album of 25 April 2016, produced by Col Bennett, with artwork by James White. [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/11581585-FM-84-Atlas).
James White, who works as Signalnoise, also made the key art for *Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon* ([record](ref:far-cry-3-blood-dragon-2013)) and the GUNSHIP cover ([record](ref:gunship-album-cover-2015)).
observed: A sky of dark navy-violet with fine white and cyan stars and a soft grain fills the square.
A sun disc fills most of the frame. It shades from yellow at the top through orange and coral to hot magenta at the bottom, with a pink outer glow.
The upper half of the sun is solid. The lower half is cut by about ten horizontal dark bars, and the bars get thicker toward the bottom.
Under the sun, thin horizontal lines in pink, violet, and blue form a horizon band, like a reflection on water. There is no perspective grid.
“FM-84” sits small at the top left in a thin, wide white sans-serif.
interpretation: The cover is the motif as a logo: one sun, one gradient, and one set of cuts. The bars that widen toward the bottom give the sun a sense of sinking into the horizon.
borrow: Grade a sun from yellow to magenta from top to bottom, and cut only its lower half with bars that widen as they descend.
Keep the band name small and thin in a corner when the image is the logo.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The cover art is in copyright (James White / FM-84, 2016).
